reason: M1 is diode-connected to VSS and mainly provides a local bias/reference at net02 (or a weak clamp); removing it typically preserves the main gain path set by the VIN1/VIN2 NMOS devices and PMOS loads. Caveat: net02 may become less well-defined at DC unless it is otherwise biased through M4/M7, which can shift operating point.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (bias stability at net02 may worsen; core amplification can remain)

reason: M4 looks like an NMOS pull-down/clamp for VOUT1 controlled by net02; deleting it usually leaves the output still driven by the PMOS load (M6) and the input NMOS branch currents. Caveat: without this pull-down helper, output common-mode/discharge and negative swing may degrade, and VOUT1 could sit higher.
impact_estimate: Low (mostly affects output swing/settling, not the differential input action)

reason: M7 provides a PMOS connection from VDD into the internal node net02 driven by net030 (VIN1 side), likely for biasing/cascoding; removing it often keeps the basic VIN1/VIN2 current steering and the VOUT1 pull-up (M6) functional. Caveat: net02 biasing changes significantly, so gain/output impedance may drop and the operating point may shift.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (core function remains but gain and bias point can change)
